description: RAIN correlates utilization, clinical outcomes, social barriers, and telehealth reach across the rural counties overnight and surfaces population-level equity signals before you ask — the expanding maternal care desert, avoidable-ED concentration, and the telehealth equity gap left by the Battle Mountain closure.

A single interface reasoning across the data warehouse, claims, EHR, State HIE, SDOH, connectivity, and telehealth records at once — mapping one closure into five interconnected effects (maternal access, chronic continuity, ED utilization, transport strain, telehealth equity) that no single system would surface.

Models RHTP-aligned interventions against the cascade — mobile obstetric outreach, a telehealth connectivity bridge, and care-continuity restoration — projecting reach, timeline, cost, and outcome for each, and recommending the parallel path with the highest access and equity return.

Generates a Nevada Health Authority equity brief structured to the RHTP outcome priorities — situation, cross-system evidence, recommended interventions, projected 12-month outcomes, and a measurement plan — with a sourced county-level data appendix assembled from every contributing system.
